neighbours.label: First-person present-tense narration of a scene (on my shoulder, a dozen of us, I take in the view, I ask); the same scenes in third-person past stay quiet
fire: A monkey climbs onto my shoulder and tugs at my hair.
Our guide waves, and a handful of us follow her into the trees.
Catching my breath, I take in the view of the valley.
"Well, how was it?" I ask Anna eagerly as I sit down.
The ranger hands me a lamp and leads a dozen of us downhill.
Resting on a log, I watch the herons lift off.
The parrot lands on my wrist, pecking at my watch.
"Any luck?" I call to Sam as I wade in.
quiet: A monkey climbed onto the branch and tugged at a vine.
The guide waved, and a handful of tourists followed her into the trees.
Catching its breath, the deer stood in the valley.
"Well, how was it?" Anna asked as she sat down.
The ranger handed them a lamp and led the group downhill.
Resting on a log, the old man watched the herons lift off.
The parrot landed on the perch, pecking at a seed.
"Any luck?" Tom called to Sam as he waded in.
